questions.question: Consider the following statements : 1. The Election Commission is a constitutional body. 2. The Election Commission decides the election schedules for the conduct of elections, whether general elections or by-elections. 3. The decisions of the Election Commission cannot be challenged in the High Court. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements :

1. The Election Commission is a constitutional body.

2. The Election Commission decides the election schedules for the conduct of elections, whether general elections or by-elections.

3. The decisions of the Election Commission cannot be challenged in the High Court.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

In News

  • The opposition has questioned the impartiality of the upcoming elections in five states after Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sushil Chandra and Election Commissioners Rajiv Kumar and Anup Chandra Pandey attended an online interaction called by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Key Points

  • Election Commission:
    • The Election Commission is a constitutional authority whose responsibilities and powers are prescribed in the Constitution of India under Article 324. Hence statement 1 is correct.
    • The Election Commission is insulated from executive interference.
    • It is the Commission that decides the election schedules for the conduct of elections, whether general elections or by-elections. Hence statement 2 is correct.
    • It is the Commission that decides on the location of polling stations, assignment of voters to the polling stations, location of counting centres, arrangements to be made in and around polling stations and counting centres and all allied matters.
    • The decisions of the Commission can be challenged in the High Court and the Supreme Court of India by appropriate petitions. Hence statement 3 is not correct.
    • By long-standing convention and several judicial pronouncements, once the actual process of elections has started, the judiciary does not intervene in the actual conduct of the polls.

questions.question: In the second Round Table Conference held in 1931, which of the following freedom fighters represented Congress?
questions.questionHtml: In the second Round Table Conference held in 1931, which of the following freedom fighters represented Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

Key Points

  • Mahatma Gandhi was the sole representative of the Indian National Congress at the Second Round Table Conference held in 1931.
  • The conference was a series of three meetings in London and was part of the constitutional reform process in India.
  • It aimed to discuss the Simon Commission report and the future constitution of India.
  • Gandhi attended to negotiate the terms of Indian independence and pressed for the rights of the Indian people.
  • Despite his efforts, the conference did not lead to any significant breakthrough due to the lack of agreement between the British and Indian representatives.

Additional Information

Main Keyword Description
Round Table Conferences The series of conferences held from 1930 to 1932 aimed at discussing constitutional reforms in India, involving British and Indian officials and representatives from Indian communities.
First Conference November 1930, highlighted the absence of the Congress Party.
Second Conference September-November 1931, notable for Gandhi's participation.
Third Conference November 1932, focused on the representation of minorities and resulted in the Communal Award.
Outcome Though the conferences did not lead to immediate reforms, they were significant in the process leading to the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.question: Consider the following regarding Lodhi Dynasty- Ruler Rule (A) Bahlol Lodi (i) 1489-1517 AD (B) Sikandar Lodi (ii) 1517-1526 AD (C) Ibrahim Lodi (iii) 1451-1489 AD Match the ruler with their correct reign.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is NOT a part of the Odia culture?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dances is NOT a part of the Odia culture?
questions.solution: Kathakali is a classical dance form from Kerala, distinct from the Odia culture. In contrast, Gotipua is a traditional dance performed by young boys dressed as female dancers, Paika is a martial dance showcasing the valor of Odishan warriors, and Dalkhai is a folk dance performed during the Dussehra festival by tribal communities. Odisha is renowned for its diverse dance traditions, including the classical dance form Odissi, as well as other notable dances like Chhau and Ghumura. Kathakali is characterized by its elaborate costumes, makeup, and expressive storytelling through facial expressions.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state’?
questions.questionHtml: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state’?
questions.solution: Article 164(2) of the Indian Constitution mandates that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state. This implies that the entire Council, including the Chief Minister, must answer to the Assembly for its actions. A vote of no confidence by the Assembly necessitates the resignation of the whole Council. This ensures the executive's accountability and reflects parliamentary democracy principles. The Indian Constitution, effective from 26th January 1950, is the world's longest written constitution, detailing political principles, structures, powers, and citizen duties, and emphasizing justice, equality, and liberty.

questions.question: Consider the following pair: Festival State 1. Hornbill festival Mizoram 2. Losar Sikkim 3. Kharchi Puja Tripura Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following pair:

Festival State
1. Hornbill festival Mizoram
2. Losar Sikkim
3. Kharchi Puja Tripura

Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 and 3 only.

Key Points

  • The famous Hornbill festival is celebrated in Nagaland. Hence, pair 1 is incorrectly matched.
    • Hornbill Festival is celebrated every year in Nagaland in the first week of December every year.
    • It is one of the famous &  biggest home-bred festivals in the country.
    • The festival pays respect & gives tribute to Hornbill which is the most revered & admired bird, especially for Nagas. 
  • The Tibetan New Year, popularly known as Lossar is a festival in Sikkim which is celebrated with a lot of fervor and enthusiasm. Hence, pair 2 is correctly matched
    • A harvest festival, Lossar is a significant day among the Tibetans.
    • Also known as Gyalpo Lossar it is celebrated by visiting the monastery and after performing the rituals the people visit relatives and friends.
    • The Losar festival is also celebrated by the Monpa Tribe of Tawang and the West Kemang district of Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Kharchi Puja is a Hindu festival from Tripura. Hence, pair 3 is correctly matched
    • it's a week-long royal Puja that falls in the month of July on the eighth day of the new moon.
    • This festival is celebrated at Agartala (Puran Agartala) in the temple premises of Fourteen gods.
    • The word "Kharchi" is derived from the word "Khya" which means "Earth".
    • Kharchi Puja is basically done to worship the earth.
    • All of the rituals are of tribal origin, which includes worshipping fourteen gods and Mother Earth.
    • The Puja is performed to wash out the sins and to clean the post-menstrual phase of Mother Earth's menstruation.

questions.question: Which of the following cities of the Indus Valley civilisation was divided into three parts, i.e. the citadel, a middle town and a lower town?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following cities of the Indus Valley civilisation was divided into three parts, i.e. the citadel, a middle town and a lower town?
questions.solution: The town in Indus valley civilization was divided into two parts citadel and lower town. Unlike other towns, Dholavira has divided into three parts citadel, a middle town and a lower town with walls made of sandstone or limestone instead of mud bricks in many other Harappan sites. Dholavira is an archaeological site at Khadirbet in Bhachau Taluka of Kutch District, in the state of Gujarat in western India.

questions.question: Muhammad bin Tughluq, Sultan of the Delhi sultanate, moved his capital from Delhi to which of the following places?
questions.questionHtml: Muhammad bin Tughluq, Sultan of the Delhi sultanate, moved his capital from Delhi to which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Daulatabad.

Key Points

  • In 1327, Tughluq decided to transfer his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad in the Deccan region of India.
  • It is claimed that he instructed every last resident of Delhi to pack up and walk to the new capital.
  • Mohammad-bin-Tughlaq transferred his capital from Delhi to Devagiri to have superior administration over South India and forcibly transferred the total population to the new capital.
  • Yet the capital moved back to Delhi after two years due to the lack of water supply in Devagiri.

Additional Information

  • For, all Muhammad bin Tughluq's  works such as the transfer of capital from Delhi to Daulatabad, the introduction of token currency, an experiment in Doab and the expedition to Kangra were all failed.
  • Mohammad bin Tughlaq was the king of Delhi between 1325 to 1351. 
  • Muhammad bin Tughluq was the eldest son of Ghiyas-ud-Din-Tughlaq, the originator of the Tughlaq dynasty.​

    • India produced 150.18 million tonnes of rice, becoming the world leader.
    • China’s rice production stood at 145.28 million tonnes.
  • Improved Crop Varieties
    • 184 new varieties unveiled covering cereals, pulses, oilseeds, fodder crops, sugarcane, cotton, jute, and tobacco.

questions.question: How many minutes is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
questions.questionHtml: How many minutes is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 40 minutes.
Key Points
  • Kabaddi is a popular contact sport in South Asia.
  • It is played between two teams of 7 players each.
  • The objective of the game is for a player, known as a raider, to cross into the opposing team's half and tag as many defenders as possible before returning to their own half.
  • A match consists of two halves, each lasting 20 minutes (total 40 minutes), with a break of 5 minutes in between.
  • Kabaddi is also known as hu-tu-tu in western India, ha-do-do in eastern India and Bangladesh, chedu-gudu in southern India, gudu in Sri Lanka, and theechub in Thailand.

Additional InformationTime duration for different sports:

Football 90 ( 2 halves of 45 minutes) 15-minute rest period in between called halftime.
Field Hockey 60 ( 4 quarters of 15 minutes) 2 minutes break after the first and third quarter and a 15 minutes-interval after the second quarter, which is halftime.
Kabaddi 40 ( two halves of 20 minutes) A 5 minutes break between halves.
Basketball 48 ( four quarters of 12 minutes) 2.5 minutes break after the first and third quarter and a 15 minutes-interval after the second quarter, which is halftime.
Boxing 4 to 12 rounds of 3 minutes each.  
Freestyle wrestling 6 ( 2 periods of 3 minutes) 30 seconds break in between.

options.text: They ensure social and economic development.
options.html: They ensure social and economic development.

options.text: They provide guidelines for the governance of the country.
options.html: They provide guidelines for the governance of the country.

options.text: They are morally binding on the government.
options.html: They are morally binding on the government.

questions.solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are guidelines enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, aimed at promoting social and economic justice. They ensure social and economic development by guiding the state in formulating policies for the welfare of the people. The DPSPs provide a framework for governance, directing the government in law and policy-making to promote public welfare.
